transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alice Morgan (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Cho (PioneerMed), Marcus Reilly (PioneerMed), Sofia Patel (PioneerMed security)

[00:00] Alice: hi everyone thanks for joining, quick check-in today, main agenda — renewal timing and regional uplift, and any security blockers.
[00:22] Marcus: yeah thanks Alice, we've got Q2 budget cycles closing, want to lock a path for EU and APAC activation and a small dedicated pool for critical inference.
[00:36] Diego: cool, quick clarification — when you say dedicated pool, are you thinking reserved capacity 24/7 or burstable reserved?
[00:45] Marcus: primarily reserved 24/7 for our patient-facing routing models, maybe burst for batch scoring. latency is important for the routing stuff.
[00:58] Dr. Cho: also want to understand how much latency improvement we get vs hosted. your benchmark doc showed global P50 improvements but our real world p90s matter.
[01:12] Alice: totally. dedicated will drop p90 substantially for us because of Affinity and the KV cache optimizations — though sometimes the transcript wrote KV cash in our docs so sorry for the typo — but we can run a short latency bench with your payload.
[01:29] Sofia: security first — SOC 2 is fine but we need KMS/HSM support for key separation, plus an SSO flow with Okta and RBAC mapping. is that all supported in private / vpc?
[01:44] Diego: Yes, VPC + Private control plane supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integration, and SAML/Okta. We do have a config readout for RBAC mapping—I'll send our template. small caveat: the on-prem package has an extra ops lead time.
[02:01] Marcus: ops lead time — how long? we have a go/no-go in 6 weeks ideally.
[02:08] Diego: For a VPC + KMS integration and dedicated nodes, the typical runway is 3–5 weeks if credentials and network peering are ready; on-prem (air gap) is more like 6–8.
[02:24] Alice: and for EU activation we can do staged activation — start with hosted endpoints in eu-west, then switch traffic to dedicated safety nodes once the VPC is up.
[02:37] Dr. Cho: ok, cost question — you're going to suggest quantization and batching on the dedicated pool to manage tokens costs?
[02:45] Diego: yes, we recommend a mixed strategy: slightly lower quantization for latency-critical models, aggressive quantization for background batch scoring. Also prefix caching reduces tokens on repeated context — though caching effectiveness depends on your prompt churn.
[03:03] Marcus: competitor question — MegaML suggested using their managed endpoints for EU and told us they'd waive egress for first year. any differentiator?
[03:12] Alice: Main diffs: Redwood gives the same API across hosted/dedicated/private so your devs don't rewire code during migrations; plus we provide cost/perf tooling in Console and rollout policies. Also our SLAs for dedicated are explicit. We'll send a comparative note.
[03:30] Sofia: earlier you mentioned audit logs — are we able to keep token-level logs for 90 days? we might need 365 for compliance.
[03:40] Diego: Console can retain higher fidelity logs as an add-on; 90 is the default, 365 is available as premium add-on with redaction options for PHI. We'll include privacy/redaction notes in the security doc.
[03:56] Alice: great. next up — timeline. Marcus, you mentioned 6 weeks. if we align, we'd want signed amendment and PO in that window. Is procurement in flight?
[04:08] Marcus: Procurement needs updated pricing and a simple amendment to add eu/apac and 2 dedicated nodes — they're the blockers.
[04:18] Alice: ok we'll produce two pricing scenarios: A) minimal hosted + EU/APAC activation with burstable capacity, B) reserved dedicated pool (2 nodes) + EU/APAC + VPC. We'll show estimated monthly delta and a 12-month committed price.
[04:32] Dr. Cho: can you also model p90 improvements? even ballpark helps.
[04:38] Diego: yes we'll run a short bench on a sample payload, simulate p90; if you can share a 1k-2k request sample we'll run perf tests on both hosted and a dedicated test instance.
[04:52] Marcus: we can do that, I'll ask devs to scrub data and share traces.
[05:00] Sofia: note — if we move PHI through logs we need client-side redaction. is there an SDK hook?
[05:07] Diego: SDK has pre-send hooks; many customers do client-side redaction. We'll point to examples.
[05:16] Dr. Cho: good. any blockers on routing policies — we need canary for EU cutover.
[05:22] Alice: Console supports canary rollouts, traffic percentage controls, automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated nodes return errors. We'll include a brief runbook.
[05:33] Marcus: one more — pricing cadence, do we do monthly or annual commit? procurement leans to annual but wants a mid-year review.
[05:41] Alice: both supported; annual gives discount. We'll show both numbers and renewal amendment language for mid-year review.
[05:50] (crosstalk)
[06:00] Alice: recap — Redwood to send pricing scenarios and security pack (SOC2, KMS notes, RBAC playbook), Diego to run benchmark once PioneerMed provides sample requests, Marcus to confirm procurement timeline, and schedule follow-up benchmark call week of 3/27.
[06:20] Marcus: sounds good.
[06:24] Dr. Cho: thank you, appreciated.
[06:27] Alice: thanks all, we'll follow up by next week.
End transcript.

Notes: occasional auto-transcription oddities — product names spelled "Red wood" or "Redwood Dedicate" in some voice-to-text lines.
